name: Needed file among the first three files a builder's cards show (finding a file)
purpose: A floor for finding one file: it judges how a store of cards leads a fixed selector to a single needed file. It favours a card per file by construction, so it never selects a topic-card builder; per_file_symbols and the degenerate groupings are its baselines.
record: Per builder, the balanced score (accuracy, cost and time; [balance.cards_from_files]). A case passes when the needed file is among the first three files of the view the fixed selector renders: the picked cards in rank order, each card's files in the builder's own order, as production renders them without a per-query reordering. In the details: the same within the first ten files, the needed file anywhere in the view, the median and largest view in files, cards built, the build's id, its model calls, tokens, cost and seconds (charged to the first scored case).
disadvantages: The cases ask about one Python repository, so a builder good at prose folders is not measured; the selector is keyword IDF, not production's hybrid, because the vector half needs an authorized embedding run; a grouped card wins only if its builder orders its files well, because the selector already ranks one-file cards per question, so this stage favours the per-file floor and only a stage where a model reads the rendered view can show what grouping adds; one build is spread over the cases of one run, while a real build serves many more turns, so the price a model builder pays here is an upper bound. Because the target is one file, a card per file wins it; that is why this metric is a floor and the topic-needs metric decides.

name: Needed files of a piece of work inside the first cards a builder's store gives
purpose: A card groups information on one topic from many files, so a card builder is judged by whether the top cards of a topic task hold the files the work needed, from a store small enough to be topic cards and at a price a team would pay.
record: Per builder, the balanced score (accuracy, cost and time; [balance.needed_set]). Tasks from Quest AI Runner's git history whose subject names no file or identifier; the files of the commit that are in the pinned corpus are the needed set. The history is cut in time: a builder may learn only from commits older than every task. A case passes when at least half of the needed files are inside the first three cards the fixed selector picks and those cards hold at most 30 files. In the details: the share of the needed files in the first card (cov1) and in the first three (cov3), the share of those files that are not needed (noise3), how often a card bundled files of two folders when the task spans them (bundled), the cards built and the cards per file. A store above 0.25 cards per file is disqualified (a balanced score of zero): the Quest store keeps at most 1,000 cards and a card per file is an index of files.
disadvantages: Subjects are developer language written for a commit; some files were renamed later; the corpus is the pinned state while the tasks are earlier; the selector is keyword IDF, not production's hybrid; coverage is the right files in front of the reader, not an answer found; the balanced score has no store-size term of its own, so the cap is a gate and not a weight.

name: Folder of the needed file among the first files a builder's cards show
purpose: A proxy, free and with no model, for the part of what topic cards are for that a single-file target cannot show: putting a reader in the right part of the code.
record: Per builder, the balanced score ([balance.orientation]). For each of the file-finding tasks of the file-finding metric, a case passes when one of the first three files of the view is in the target's own folder. In the details: the area hits (the first card's files share the target's folder or its parent) and the build.
disadvantages: It measures nearness and not that a reader found anything; it favours a card per file because the target is one file; it is a proxy and decides nothing alone.
